sentences.text: Then Mahesh Sahni started playing a recording of him talking indecently to me and threatening to make the recording viral.

The victim at the relevant point of time was aged 20 years and happens to be the niece of the Respondent No.2.

In pursuance of the Notice issued by this Court, the State has filed its counter affidavit dated 25-8-2025.

6.
Upon the registration of the subject FIR, multiple attempts (raids) were conducted by the police to arrest Respondent No. 2, however, he remained absconding.
Owing to the same, non bailable warrant was issued by the Ld. Trial Court on 20.10.2024 that could not be executed as Respondent No. 2 remained absconding.

Thereafter, proclamation orders were also obtained from the Ld. Trial Court against Respondent No. 2 under section 82 CrPC on 29.01.2025 and the same were executed/affixed on 06.02.2025.
10.
Since Respondent No. 2 has not cooperated with the investigation, the allegations regarding him blackmailing the Petitioner using audio recordings have not been verified from the accused.

However, on the basis of the statement of the Petitioner and other evidence, a chargesheet bearing X vs The State Of Bihar on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81652435/

sentences.text: 9. We wonder whether all the relevant facts were brought to the notice of the High Court at the time of hearing of the anticipatory bail application.
10. Unfortunately, the impugned order passed by the High Court is very cryptic.

11. We do not want to say anything further as we are inclined to set aside the impugned order passed by the High Court and remit the matter to the High Court for fresh hearing of the anticipatory bail application.
12. In such circumstances, referred to above, this appeal is partly allowed.
13. The impugned Order passed by the High Court is set aside.
14. The matter is remitted to the High Court.
15. The High Court shall hear the Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.4149/2025 filed by the accused afresh on its own merits in accordance with law.
16. Before hearing the application afresh, the High Court shall call for an appropriate report from the Investigating Officer.
After hearing all the parties concerned, the High Court shall proceed to pass an appropriate order in accordance with law.

17. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
